title: Personalise the #greeting heading from a ?name= query parameter
spec: Change only src/main.ts. Today the import side effect always writes greeting("world") into h1#greeting. Instead, read the `name` query parameter from the page URL (URLSearchParams over location.search, so percent-encoding is decoded) and write greeting(name) into #greeting. If the parameter is missing, empty, or whitespace-only, fall back to greeting("world"). Keep writing through textContent (never innerHTML): the name is untrusted input and must render as literal text. Keep the exported greeting(name: string): string signature and behaviour unchanged; this is not a public_api change. Constraint from the c-001 characterization tests (e2e/greeting.spec.ts): they import src/main.ts in Node with a stubbed `document` and no `location`/`window` global, and expect the import to query '#greeting' exactly once and set 'Hello, world!'. So the URL read must not throw when `location` is undefined (e.g. `globalThis.location?.search ?? ""`) and must fall back to world there. The full suite `npx playwright test` (c-001 + this card) must stay green, and `npm run build` and `npm run lint` must pass. No new dependencies. risk_class is medium: the manifest risk_class is medium and the change touches no owner_approval.required_for category (new_dependency).
